phase: Phase S3: Structured output for the evaluation features
summary: Second review round at 8eee12fc. The audited HEAD is current and provenance-bound. Applicability stays applicable: the remediation edits an untrusted response-body field that reaches a console log. The prior blocking finding F1 is remediated and I withdraw it. structured.ts reuses the one exported safeModel validator from providers.ts on every console path: the served-model read (structured.ts:223), the error-path usage record (structured.ts:240), and the final usage record (structured.ts:253). The failing-first R-B1 test proves a key-shaped served model records model null and never reaches any console line, and a valid model passes through. The charset-invalid case gives null through the same MODEL_ID regex (providers.ts:212, providers.ts:218-219), because the helper reuses the one validator and adds no second implementation. I checked every console path of the structured flow: retry.ts holds no console call, usage-log.ts prints record fields and the role-not-configured line only, the structured client wires no debug logger (structured.ts:150-153), and the two BM2 callers log nothing. The non-enumerable requireParameters key is safe: the helper builds it from a hardcoded literal (structured.ts:166-170), no untrusted input reaches it, the key holds the constant true, serialization skips non-enumerable keys, and the R-A1 test drives the real SDK with a mocked fetch and proves the wire body carries provider.require_parameters true. My heavy-runs at HEAD pass every group: the remediation group passes 2, the full ai-tutoring package passes 158 of 158, the BM2 no-PII release-gate group passes 3, the BM2 S3 fix group passes 2, and the IM3 S3 fix group passes 7. The five earlier findings and the BM2 PII release gate show no regression. F2 to F4 were declined as carried debt; the three entries exist in measure/tech-debt.md and I still judge them nonblocking for the BM2 student-release gate. No blocking finding stands, so the gate passes.
nonblocking_findings: F2 (carried debt, recorded in measure/tech-debt.md line 64; still nonblocking for the BM2 student-release gate): stripPersonDetails removes each known account value at any length (lesson-context.ts:89-92), and BM2 convex auth accepts a username with no length floor (convex/auth.ts:117). A one- or two-character username deletes substrings from lesson math in the prompt. No leak occurs; only prompt text quality degrades.

F3 (carried debt, recorded in measure/tech-debt.md line 65; still nonblocking): the BM2 student lesson-chatbot rate-limit catch logs a fixed status null (route.ts:101-105). No leak occurs; the log cannot name the failure status.

F4 (carried debt, recorded in measure/tech-debt.md line 66; still nonblocking): the teacher ai-error-summary outer catch still logs the raw error object (route.ts:137). The structured helper never throws, so the error holds Convex and mapping text only, and the route is teacher-authed. No leak occurs.

No production source changed in the Red commit 36b27a50.

Charset-invalid case: MODEL_ID accepts only 1 to 128 chars of the bounded set (providers.ts:212), so any other string gives null through the one safeModel (providers.ts:218-219). structured.ts imports that one validator (structured.ts:12) and adds no second implementation, so the key-shaped and charset-invalid rules of the chat path hold on the structured path by the same code object.

Provider preference is injection-safe: the helper builds it from a hardcoded literal with Object.defineProperty (structured.ts:166-170). No untrusted input flows into the object. The added key holds the constant true, so it holds no secret. Serialization skips non-enumerable keys, so the SDK boundary keeps only require_parameters (the boundary assertion at structured.test.ts:103-118 still passes), and the R-A1 test with the real SDK and a mocked fetch proves the wire body carries provider.require_parameters true (structured.test.ts:236-296).
